body.v: Your parcel from an overseas shop has arrived in Switzerland. A customs handling charge of CHF 3.20 is due before delivery.
Once paid, your parcel will be delivered within two working days.

hotspots.explain: parcelpoint-delivery.example is not ParcelPoint's domain, parcelpoint.example. It is the only slip in the whole email.
No deadline, no threat, no typos. A scam does not have to shout.
The link matches the sender, but both are on the lookalike domain. Matching each other does not make them real.
A small fee, so you will not think twice about paying. The payment page would take your card details.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone pretending to be ParcelPoint. Every detail is right except the domain: parcelpoint-delivery.example is not parcelpoint.example.
choices: ParcelPoint, because everything else is right

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Hardly any. It is calm and routine, which makes it easier to trust.
choices: Very little: it is calm and routine

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Pay a small charge through a link. That would hand your card details to whoever wrote it.
choices: Pay a small charge through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the ParcelPoint app, or type its address yourself, and see whether a charge is really due.
choices: Reply to ask for the customs form

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and check for a charge
actions.consequence: No charge is listed. The email was fake.

actions.label: Pay the CHF 3.20, because it is so small
actions.consequence: Your card details go to the scammer. Small fees are how they get them.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
Reply and ask for the customs form
actions.consequence: The scammer sends you a fake form. Your reply also shows your address is in use.

attacker_reveal: No rush, no typos, no threats... Surface clues are for beginners. A calm email on a lookalike domain beats a loud one every time.
